fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.

• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges to maintain a clear path for emergency vehicles from the street to the residence.

• Cut back plants and shrubs growing close to the main residence and detached structure to reduce the spread of fire between vegetation and buildings.

• Keep a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing accessible from the front to allow responders to reach the rear of the property on foot.

• Mark any rear gate or secondary entry point with a reflective sign or address placard so responders can locate it without searching.

• Store a spare key or install a lockbox at the front entrance so responders can access the property without forced entry.

• Keep the walkway and patio area clear of stored items, furniture, or equipment that would block responder movement around the structure.

• Thin dense vegetation between the detached structure and the main residence so responders can move between the two buildings without obstruction.

• Maintain the open lawn area free of parked vehicles or stored materials that would block a staging area for emergency equipment.

• Because the property has only one vehicle access point, keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles at all times to allow emergency vehicles to reach and exit the property without obstruction.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster closest to the structure to increase open space between the trees and the building.
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly next to or touching the structure on any side.
• Remove low-hanging branches from trees near the structure so branches do not extend close to the roofline or walls.
• Thin mixed vegetation patches between the tree cluster and the structure to reduce the amount of connected plant material leading toward the building.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway so vehicles, including fire trucks, can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway clear of shrubs and vegetation encroaching from the sides so the full width of the travel lane remains open.
• Clear vegetation along the rear of the property to create more room for movement around the back of the structure.
• Keep the single access route free of fallen branches, overgrown vegetation, and debris so it remains passable at all times.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from shrubs and scattered trees near the structure before dry season.
• Maintain the existing open green space by preventing shrubs and scattered vegetation from spreading into it over time.
